result_text:
I changed the two mock-folder rules in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394). I did not write a test for the new cases, and I did not run any of your example paths through the rule.

- **The change:** `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` now use `[^/\\]*` after `mock`. `[^/\\]*` matches any run of characters except `/` and `\`, so the match stays inside that one folder name. A plain `mock/` folder, names with punctuation such as `mock.data` or `mock(old)`, and names with non-ASCII characters now match.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already tries each pattern against a slash-normalised copy of the path, so `a\mock\x.java` is covered without further changes.
- **What stays out of scope:** `remock/`, `demo/` and `src/main/java/` don't match, because the rule needs `/mock` at the start of a folder name. Files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` don't match either, because the rule needs a `/` after the name.
- **Previously matched folders:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still fit the new pattern.

I ran the `Scoping*Test` and `Convention*Test` classes in `codeanalyzer` and they passed. That glob may not have matched any test classes, and the run printed no test count.
